currentContext.expansion: The Company's growth during the year was largely capital-markets and sustainability-led rather than new manufacturing capacity: it migrated from the NSE SME Emerge platform to the NSE Main Board effective September 18, 2025, and subsequently listed on the BSE Main Board effective May 27, 2026, giving it dual-exchange status within roughly eight months. risks.risk: Regulatory/SEBI action involving Promoters and Directors
risks.note: The Company, its Promoters, Directors and certain other persons received a SEBI Show Cause Notice dated January 29, 2025 in connection with Mangalam Global Enterprise Limited; a Settlement Order dated March 30, 2026 has been received by the common Independent Directors, but the Company is still awaiting formal communication from SEBI, leaving the matter not fully closed as of the report date.

risks.risk: No formally constituted Risk Management Committee
risks.note: The Company states it is not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee or a formal Risk Management Policy under the Companies Act/SEBI criteria applicable to it, so risk oversight relies on the Audit Committee and Board review rather than a dedicated committee framework.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic, currency, interest-rate and competitive exposure
risks.note: Management's cautionary statement flags general market, macroeconomic, governmental and regulatory trends, movements in currency exchange and interest rates, competitive pressures and technological developments as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking expectations.
The Debt-Equity Ratio increased from 0.77 times to 0.81 times year-on-year (a 5.19% change), indicating incremental reliance on debt in the capital structure.

The Net Capital Turnover Ratio declined from 7.28 times to 4.58 times (a 37.09% decline), attributed to higher working capital deployed to support increased scale of operations, with growth in the working capital base outpacing growth in revenue.

risks.risk: Inventory build-up ahead of demand realisation
risks.note: The Inventory Turnover Ratio declined from 4.48 times to 2.84 times (a 36.61% decline), attributed to higher inventory holding to support planned scale-up of operations and to meet anticipated order book in the ensuing year — a bet on future demand that carries inventory and working-capital risk if realisation slips.

The proposed Scheme of Amalgamation of subsidiary Mangalam Saarloh Private Limited with the Company, approved by the Board in April 2023, remains pending with NSE for in-principle approval/NOC as of the report date, indicating prolonged regulatory/approval risk on corporate restructuring.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Mangalam Worldwide manufactures stainless steel (200/300/400 series and special grades like 17/4 PH, Duplex and Super Duplex) across four integrated units in Gujarat producing SS Billets & Ingots, SS Flat/Round Bars, Bright Bars, and Seamless Pipes & Tubes/U-Bend Tubes/ERW Pipes, using its own round bars and billets captively as feedstock at successive stages. Products serve food and dairy equipment, oil and gas, aerospace, medical devices, refinery and petrochemicals, power, fertilizer, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, nuclear, breweries and defense industries, with exports to about 20 countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, Russia and the Americas. The Company operates in a single reportable business/geographical segment and also trades in steel scrap and ferro alloys.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's economy expanded at one of the fastest paces among major economies in FY2025-26, propelled by government capital expenditure, resilient private consumption and a steady infrastructure investment pipeline
- India's steel sector consumption grew in high single digits even as the broader global market struggled, with crude steel capacity crossing the 200-million-tonne mark en route to an ambitious 300-million-tonne target by the turn of the decade
- Domestic stainless steel consumption is projected to rise from roughly 4.8 million tonnes toward 6 million tonnes within the next couple of years, driven by railways, metro and tunnel infrastructure, ports and airports, energy and process industries, and construction/architecture increasingly specifying stainless steel for durability and lifecycle economics
- India's per-capita stainless steel consumption remains a fraction of the developed-world average, viewed by management as headroom rather than a constraint
- Growth during the year was broad-based across quarters (revenue up 21% in Q1, 33% in Q2, 29% in Q3) with even faster profit growth, reflecting improving operating leverage and a richer product mix
- Operating margins strengthened through the year, moving from just over 7% in the opening quarter to nearly 7.6% by the third quarter, as efficiency initiatives across melting, rolling and tube-making operations compounded
- Exports grew by more than 100% year-on-year in some of the strongest quarters as the Company deepened relationships across its ~20-country customer base

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Sharpening focus on value-added, higher-margin product categories that command stronger realisations than commodity-grade output
- Directing the majority of internal accruals toward growth rather than higher payout
- Reducing face value of equity shares from Rs.10 to Re.1 (stock sub-division) to improve liquidity and broaden retail participation
- Deepening export relationships across the ~20 countries served, spanning Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, Russia and the Americas
- Investing in captive renewable (solar) power generation to reduce energy costs and carbon footprint
- Treating risk management (raw material/scrap price volatility, energy costs, trade and tariff developments) as a continuous operating discipline rather than a periodic review exercise
- Board recommended a final dividend of Re. 0.30 per equity share (face value Rs.10) for FY2025-26, up from Re. 0.20 per share in FY2024-25, subject to shareholder approval at the 30th AGM; if the pending 10-for-1 sub-division (stock split, face value Rs.10 to Re.1) is completed before the dividend is paid, the dividend will instead be paid on the sub-divided shares in a proportion that keeps each shareholder's aggregate dividend entitlement unchanged.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's growth during the year was largely capital-markets and sustainability-led rather than new manufacturing capacity: it migrated from the NSE SME Emerge platform to the NSE Main Board effective September 18, 2025, and subsequently listed on the BSE Main Board effective May 27, 2026, giving it dual-exchange status within roughly eight months. On the renewable energy side, the Company commissioned a 1,200 KWp Rooftop Solar Power Plant at its Kapadvanj (Kheda district) unit for captive consumption during the year, and separately commenced erection and installation of a larger 10.4 MW DC ground-mounted solar power plant (two 5,200 kWp DC plants) at Village Handod, Taluka Karjan, District Vadodara, on land leased for 25 years, to supply captive power to the Halol manufacturing unit. The Company's four integrated stainless-steel facilities in Gujarat (Halol - melting; Changodar - rolling; Kapadvanj - bright bar and seamless pipes/tubes) together comprise cumulatively more than 1,90,000 tonnes per annum of installed capacity, with management's stated focus on sharpening the product mix toward value-added, higher-margin categories rather than adding fresh commodity-grade capacity. The Company also raised capital via two NCD tranches aggregating Rs.100 crore (Rs.50 crore in March 2026 and Rs.50 crore in April 2026) through private placement, and post year-end approved a 10-for-1 sub-division of equity shares (face value Rs.10 to Re.1) to improve liquidity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully integrated manufacturing from scrap melting through to seamless pipes & tubes, using own round bars/billets as captive raw material to reduce costs
- Long-term trust-based relationships with customers built over past few years of scaling
- Adaptable to diverse industry segments with efficient procurement capabilities

risks.body:

- Rising financial leverage — The Debt-Equity Ratio increased from 0.77 times to 0.81 times year-on-year (a 5.19% change), indicating incremental reliance on debt in the capital structure.
- Rising working-capital intensity — The Net Capital Turnover Ratio declined from 7.28 times to 4.58 times (a 37.09% decline), attributed to higher working capital deployed to support increased scale of operations, with growth in the working capital base outpacing growth in revenue.
- Inventory build-up ahead of demand realisation — The Inventory Turnover Ratio declined from 4.48 times to 2.84 times (a 36.61% decline), attributed to higher inventory holding to support planned scale-up of operations and to meet anticipated order book in the ensuing year — a bet on future demand that carries inventory and working-capital risk if realisation slips.
- Long-pending subsidiary amalgamation — The proposed Scheme of Amalgamation of subsidiary Mangalam Saarloh Private Limited with the Company, approved by the Board in April 2023, remains pending with NSE for in-principle approval/NOC as of the report date, indicating prolonged regulatory/approval risk on corporate restructuring.
